findings.claim: Using Math.max causes reserve to return negative stock when demand exceeds availability and to consume excess stock when demand is below availability.
findings.evidence: At both pins caller.mjs:2 defines reserve(stock, requested) as stock - allowed(requested, stock). At head, reserve(3, 5) therefore returns -2 instead of base's 0, violating the explicit nonnegative-stock invariant. Head reserve(5, 2) returns 0 instead of base's 3, and reserve(5, 0) also returns 0, consuming stock despite no request. These results follow directly from the changed Math.max expression.

findings.claim: Math.max causes reserve to overdraw stock when demand exceeds stock and to over-fulfill smaller requests.
findings.evidence: At head, allowed(requested, available) returns Math.max(requested, available), and caller.mjs:2 returns stock - allowed(requested, stock). Thus reserve(3, 5) evaluates to -2, violating the nonnegative-stock invariant; reserve(5, 2) evaluates to 0 rather than 3, consuming three extra units. At base, Math.min produces 0 and 3 respectively. Restore the cap so the reserved quantity is min(requested, stock).

adjudication.reason: Changed Math.max causes overdraw/overfulfillment in unchanged caller.mjs:2; base satisfies contract.
